claims.text: Adding approximately 5 at% Nb to a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy will promote Nb-rich precipitation.
The Nb-rich precipitates will be fine and uniformly distributed.
The Nb-rich precipitates may have a Ni3Nb-like structure.
The Nb-rich precipitates will improve elevated-temperature yield strength.
The Nb-rich precipitates will improve elevated-temperature creep resistance.
The baseline titanium- and nickel-primary HEA has a single-phase solid-solution microstructure.
The intervention is an approximately 5 at% Nb addition, with the other elemental fractions adjusted to retain an equiatomic or near-equiatomic HEA composition.
The proposed performance regime is approximately 700–1100 °C in an inert or controlled atmosphere.
Conventional thermal processing can be used to homogenize the proposed alloy.
Nb acts as a secondary-phase former in the proposed titanium-nickel matrix.
The Nb addition will produce nanoscale precipitates in situ.
The precipitates will hinder dislocation motion through precipitation hardening.
The Nb-derived precipitates will improve microstructural stability at high temperature.
At elevated temperature, the Nb-added alloy will have greater yield strength than the otherwise corresponding Nb-free alloy.
At elevated temperature, the Nb-added alloy will have better creep resistance than the otherwise corresponding Nb-free alloy.
Every constituent must remain between 5 and 35 at%, with Nb held near 5 at%.
Precipitate morphology, size, and distribution may depend on processing and heat-treatment parameters.
The Nb addition may involve trade-offs in ductility or oxidation resistance.

A controlled comparison will use identically cast and heat-treated baseline and 5 at% Nb-added samples, characterize phases by TEM, SEM, and XRD, and measure tensile and creep behavior at about 900 °C.

The hypothesis is falsified if the Nb-added alloy lacks a statistically significant improvement in yield strength and creep resistance, or if fine, uniformly distributed Nb-rich precipitates are not observed.
